description:
New Orleans' climate history, focusing on its unique geography, climate normals, flooding risks, and adaptation strategies. The video explains the city's subtropical climate shaped by the Gulf of Mexico, Mississippi River, and Lake Pontchartrain, and delves into climate normals, historical climate changes, and various flood hazards including pluvial, river, storm surge, and compound flooding. It discusses the impacts of Hurricane Katrina and the city's current protection systems, highlighting residual risks and the need for layered adaptation strategies.

Report sources:
https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/products/land-based-station/us-climate-normals
https://mpdap.coastal.la.gov/dataset/
https://www.weather.gov/lix/newnormals

title: New Orleans Climate History and Outlook
